title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Dishonesty by Client - Concealing Assets
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A client is facing a $35,000 Small Claims judgment against them. They consult a paralegal on how to legally shield their assets, but mention they are going to transfer their cottage into their sister's name to intentionally defraud the judgment creditor. What must the paralegal do?
options: Assist in drafting the transfer since the cottage is technically out of Small Claims jurisdiction.
Advise the client that this constitutes a fraudulent conveyance and the paralegal cannot assist; if the client persists, the paralegal must withdraw.
Report the client's planned fraudulent conveyance to the judgment creditor immediately.
Suggest the client use a shell corporation instead to make it harder to trace.
questions.explain: Rule 2.02 (Honesty and Candour). A paralegal shall not knowingly assist or encourage any dishonesty, fraud, crime, or illegal conduct. The paralegal must advise the client that the act is unlawful. If the client refuses to change course, Rule 8.02 requires mandatory withdrawal. Confidentiality prevents tipping off the creditor.
